speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; could you tell me how long you have had these symptoms?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, ESR, CRP
REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL; ESR: Not available in data; CRP: Not available in data; Blood_Culture: Pending at the time of examination.

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The presence of painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the wrists alongside systemic symptoms like fever and chills is highly specific. Have you noticed if these skin lesions appear on other parts of your body, such as your ankles, knees, or elbows?

REQUEST TEST: Joint_Aspiration_Left_Wrist
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_Scan_Wrists

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Joint_Aspiration_Left_Wrist: WBC >50,000 /μL (markedly elevated), Gram_Stain: Gram-negative diplococci seen; Dermatology_Scan_Wrists: Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions noted on the dorsum of both wrists and hands; two lesions on the left palm.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Septic Arthritis of the left wrist secondary to Meningococcemia (Neisseria meningitidis).
